text:
New task — prototype the cards/ companion file pattern on 3 existing wiki entries.

## What we're building

A three-tier context system for the wiki:
- **Index** (per-directory INDEX.md) — "what exists here?" ~1 line per entry
- **Card** (cards/<name>.md) — "what does this say?" Queryable surrogate. ~30 lines. Enough to answer most Protocol B queries without loading the full entry.
- **Full entry** (existing files) — "show me everything." Unchanged.

## Your task

Pick 3 entries that represent different shapes — one pattern, one gotcha, one process entry. Read each full entry. For each, create a card file at `wiki/<subdir>/cards/<same-filename>.md`.

## Card format

```yaml
---
title: "<entry title>"
id: wiki-<number>
directory: <patterns|gotchas|process|observations|findings|decisions|contracts|references>
status: <active|disputed|archived>
confidence: <high|medium|speculative>
source-agents: [<list>]
discovered: <ISO date>
last-verified: <ISO date>
related: [<list of related entry filenames>]
tags: [<lowercase, relevant keywords>]
---

## TLDR

<2-3 sentences. The claim, not the evidence.>

## Key ideas

<Bullet list, 5-8 items. Each bullet is one transferable insight — enough for an agent to answer "what is this pattern?" or "does this gotcha apply to my situation?" without loading the full entry.>
```

## Constraints

- Same filename as the full entry, just lives in cards/ subdirectory
- Create the cards/ subdirectories as needed
- Don't modify the full entries
- Keep each card under 40 lines
- The YAML frontmatter should be greppable — standardized field names, consistent value formats
- Pull metadata from the existing entry's frontmatter where it exists; infer from content where it doesn't

## After creating all 3

Send me the 3 file paths + a brief note on what you learned — was the format natural to produce? Did any field feel forced? Did any entry resist the card shape?
